alert-types.title: Google Workspace Alert types reference (Admin console)

alert_id.format: A UUID string, unique per alert.

examples.note: alertId, and the same value under metadata.alertId and id

create_time.format: An RFC3339 UTC timestamp with microsecond precision.

start_time.format: An RFC3339 UTC timestamp with microsecond precision.

end_time.format: An RFC3339 UTC timestamp with microsecond precision; absent on an ongoing alert.

update_time.format: An RFC3339 UTC timestamp with microsecond precision.

examples.note: updateTime, and the same value under metadata.updateTime

customer_id.format: An opaque per-customer string, not a human-readable name.

examples.note: customerId, and the same value under metadata.customerId and vendor_account

etag.format: A short base64-looking token; changes whenever the alert or its metadata is updated.

examples.note: etag, and the same value under metadata.etag

status.format: One fixed word from AlertMetadata's status vocabulary.
status.quote: The current status of the alert.

NOT_STARTED.meaning: No one has begun working the alert.

IN_PROGRESS.meaning: An assignee is actively working the alert.

CLOSED.meaning: Work on the alert is finished.

severity.format: One fixed word; empty when Alert Center could not determine a severity. The metadata.severity column carries the raw upper-case value; severity is a lower-cased copy.

cim_alert_kind.format: One fixed word from the Alerts data model's own type vocabulary; not an Alert Center value.

alert.meaning: A general alert record; what this sourcetype's seeded record carries.

event.meaning: A plain event, not itself an alarm or task.

task.meaning: A task raised for someone to act on.

unknown.meaning: The type could not be determined.

alert_type.format: A short English phrase naming the alert type, for example Phishing reclassification.

examples.note: event_type, signature and signature_id on the seeded record

Malware reclassification.meaning: A malware message was detected and removed after delivery.

Phishing reclassification.meaning: A phishing message was detected and removed after delivery.

Suspicious message reported.meaning: A user or automated scan flagged a message as suspicious.

User reported phishing.meaning: A user reported a message as phishing.

User reported spam spike.meaning: A spike in user-reported spam for the domain.

description.format: A full English sentence describing what the alert type means or what action Alert Center took.

examples.value: Unopened messages that are detected as phishing post-delivery are automatically reclassified and removed from the user's inbox.

dest_type.format: A short lower-case word naming the kind of destination object.

src_type.format: A short lower-case word naming the kind of source object.

examples.note: anonymized by Google's own sample; dest, user and data.messages{}.recipient all carry this value

user_name.format: A display name string; not populated on the one seeded record.

src.format: The alert's actor object, however the add-on's mapping represents it; not populated on the one seeded record.

src_ip.format: An IPv4 or IPv6 address, by CIM convention; not populated on the one seeded record.

src_user.format: An account identifier, by CIM convention; not populated on the one seeded record.

app.format: A fixed product-name string; observed constant across the seeded record.

reporting_system.format: One of a short list of Alert Center subsystem names.

examples.note: observed doubled (multivalue) on the seeded record, a double-load artifact of this dev environment

reporting_system.quote: Supported sources are any of the following

Google Operations.meaning: Google-initiated operational notices about the customer's domain.

Mobile device management.meaning: Alerts from Endpoint/mobile device management, such as a compromised device.

Gmail phishing.meaning: Alerts from Gmail's phishing, malware and spam detection.

Data Loss Prevention.meaning: Alerts from a Data Loss Prevention rule match.

Domain wide takeout.meaning: Alerts about a customer-wide data export (takeout).

State sponsored attack.meaning: Google's warning of a suspected government-backed attack on the account.

Google identity.meaning: Alerts about sign-in and account security, such as a suspicious login.

Apps outage.meaning: Alerts about a Google Workspace service outage.

payload_type.format: A type.googleapis.com URL naming the data object's proto message.

system_action.format: One fixed word from MailPhishing's systemActionType vocabulary.

NO_OPERATION.meaning: No action was taken on the message.

REMOVED_FROM_INBOX.meaning: The message was removed from the inbox.

malicious_sender.format: An email address taken from the message's own From header.

message_time.format: An RFC3339 UTC timestamp with microsecond precision.

message_subject_hash.format: A 32-character hex MD5 digest; only present for user-reported messages.

attachment_hash.format: A 64-character hex SHA256 digest, one per attachment or MIME part.
